chordInfo.name: Minor Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Explore emotional depth and melancholic beauty with minor chords - the expressive counterpart to major harmony.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: A three-note triad built by stacking a minor third (3 semitones) and a major third (4 semitones) above a root note, providing introspective and poignant harmonic resonance.

fundamentals.label: Formula
fundamentals.value: Root + Minor 3rd (3 semitones) + Perfect 5th (7 semitones). The lowered third degree (flat 3rd) creates the distinctive melancholic sound.

fundamentals.label: Interval Pattern
fundamentals.value: 3 semitones from root to third, followed by 4 semitones from third to fifth, inverting the interval order of a major triad.

fundamentals.label: Sound Quality
fundamentals.value: Characterized by emotional depth, introspection, and harmonic weight, serving as the counterweight to major harmony.

fundamentals.label: Harmonic Function
fundamentals.value: Functions as the tonic (i) in minor keys, or as secondary diatonic chords (ii, iii, vi) in major keys, creating poignant harmonic variation.

applications.label: Rock & Metal
applications.value: Drives dark riff structures and soaring power ballads, frequently utilizing the vi chord in modern rock arrangements.

applications.label: Blues & Soul
applications.value: Serves as the foundation for minor blues progressions (like i–iv–v), amplifying emotional tension and vocal sorrow.

applications.label: Pop & Neo-Soul
applications.value: Provides the essential emotional pivot point in four-chord progressions, most notably the transition to the vi relative minor.

applications.label: Classical & Film
applications.value: Establishes dramatic tension, sorrowful character themes, and mysterious ambient textures in cinematic scoring.

boxes.title: A Minor Triad Construction
items: Root: A (1st scale degree establishing the minor tonal center)
Minor 3rd: C (3rd scale degree, 3 semitones above root, creating the minor tonality)
Perfect 5th: E (5th scale degree, 7 semitones above root, anchoring acoustic stability)
Interval Stacking: Root to Minor 3rd (3 semitones) plus Minor 3rd to Perfect 5th (4 semitones)
Acoustic Result: Dark, emotionally resonant triad with strong acoustic reinforcement

boxes.title: Harmonic Character
items: Minor 3rd Interval: Distinctive interval that evokes reflective, sorrowful, or dramatic auditory perception
Consonant Foundation: Stable fifth ensures the chord remains pure rather than dissonant
Emotional Palette: Can sound somber, contemplative, fierce, or elegant depending on tempo and context
Relative Harmony: Shares two common tones with its relative major (C major shares C and E with A minor)
Voice Leading: Smoothly connects back to major tonic centers via step-wise motion

boxes.title: Scale Relationship
items: Natural Minor Degrees: Built directly from scale degrees 1, 3, and 5 of the Aeolian (natural minor) scale
Diatonic Context: Naturally occurs on degrees ii, iii, and vi in any major key
Relative Minor: Every major scale has a relative minor starting on the 6th degree (e.g., C major / A minor)
Minor Keys: Forms the primary tonic (i), subdominant (iv), and natural minor dominant (v) chords
CAGED Adaptation: Minor barre forms based on Em and Am open shapes allow moveable positioning across the neck

items: Root Position: A-C-E (root in bass)
First Inversion: C-E-A (3rd in bass)

Voice Leading: Smoother minor progressions
Bass Lines: Melodic minor movement
